title: mergecap: Option to inhibit adding capture comment

notes.body: This reads more like a bug report. Can you rephrase to describe just what this option does?

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/20868/diffs?diff_id=1588188003&start_sha=0afdcdaa1e86fc68f6e1dea4c978876ccc386a7d#28762883b9e9b4038c565c861917af29da17f127_167_165)

added 1287 commits
  • 0afdcdaa...ac7e1e82 - 1286 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • 8477fce5 - mergecap: Option to inhibit adding capture comment
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/20868/diffs?diff_id=1588188003&start_sha=0afdcdaa1e86fc68f6e1dea4c978876ccc386a7d)

Two questions this brings up:

1. Should there be pcapng blocks to record the full history of the file, so the information about every program that processed the file can be recorded (at minimum, the `shb_userappl` string for each applications that processed it, and an indication of what role that application played, e.g. "created", "filtered out packets", "merged files", "did XXX editcap transformation", etc., even if that indication is just a text string for human reader purposes - and possibly also the `shb_hardware` and `shb_os` strings, along with an indication of the input byte order)?
2. Should there be a "comment continuation from previous comment" option, to allow larger comments?

 for writing. The type given takes precedence over the extension of __outfile__.
 --
 
+--no-merging-comment::
++
+--
+Inhibit generating the capture comment "File created by merging:...". to the
+output file
+
+By default a multiline capture comment is generated to the output (merged)
+file that lists all of the files being merged. However, if the generated capture
+comment is longer than 65535 bytes it is silently dropped.
+--
+
